_comment: EXAMPLE ONLY - this file is inert where it sits.
SDLE reads exactly one policy override, at
.sdle/policies/governance-policy.json
and nothing else. Copy this file there to activate it; leaving it in
docs/ has no effect on any workflow. Strip the `_`-prefixed keys when
you do - they are commentary, not policy.
An override is MONOTONE: it may only make governance stricter. Six
weakening shapes are refused `policy_weakens_baseline` - you cannot
lower a signal weight, raise a threshold, remove a hard floor, demote a
floor's level, or drop a required gate. The built-in is the weakest
admissible policy, which is why an absent file is safe and a malformed
one is refused rather than silently defaulted.
How much you must repeat depends on the key's type, and the difference
is easy to get wrong:
LIST-valued keys - hard_floors, required_gates_always, blocking_checks
- are compared whole. Omit an entry and it reads as a removal, and the
policy is refused. Repeat the built-in verbatim, then add.
DICT-valued keys - risk_signals, risk_thresholds, required_gates_by_risk,
required_gates_by_type - MERGE entry by entry. So
{"policyVersion":"1","risk_thresholds":{"HIGH":4}} is a complete and
accepted override; the other three thresholds keep their built-in values.
optional_checks is a list whose comparison runs the other way: adding to
it is a weakening and is refused, emptying it is a tightening.
The blocks below repeat the built-in dictionaries in full anyway. That is
harmless and shows the real values beside the changed one, but it is not
required for a dictionary - only for a list.
Generate the current baseline with `sdle governance policy` rather than
copying it from here: this file was written by hand once and six signal
weights were wrong, and the engine refused every one.
Only these top-level keys may appear: policyVersion, blocking_checks,
optional_checks, risk_signals, risk_thresholds, hard_floors,
required_gates_always, required_gates_by_risk, required_gates_by_type.
`quality_checks` is deliberately not overridable - the twelve check ids
are the contract's, and a repository that could rename or drop one would
be editing the contract rather than tightening it.
Verify any override with `sdle governance policy`, which prints the
effective policy or refuses with the exact clause that weakened it.
_example_1_lower_the_bar_for_HIGH: Built-in thresholds: LOW 0, MEDIUM 2, HIGH 5, CRITICAL 9.
A LOWER number makes a level EASIER to reach, so lowering is a
tightening and is permitted; raising one is refused. Here HIGH is
_example_2_add_a_hard_floor_for_your_own: A hard floor sets a minimum risk level regardless of the computed
score, and Claude cannot lower one. The twelve built-ins are repeated
below unchanged; the last entry is the addition.
_example_3_add_a_risk_signal: A floor can only key on a signal the policy knows, so a new floor
usually needs a new signal. Weights feed the score that the thresholds
turn into a level. Every built-in weight is repeated at its exact
value - lowering any one of them is refused.
_example_4_require_a_gate_at_a_lower_ris: Built-in MEDIUM requires gate_tasks and gate_design. Adding to a level
is a tightening; removing is refused. Here MEDIUM also requires the
security gate, so anything above LOW gets a security review.
You cannot make a gate optional this way. The flow's final gate before
`complete` is always required by a derived positional rule that lives
in no dictionary, so an override cannot reach it.
